A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboBench, retaining its five dimensions, 25 tasks and core world-simulator framework. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are available for reliable comparison despite substantial revision and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 14 MLLMs in Tables 3–6, planning-error analyses and a human-alignment study.

after.justification: v2 reports evaluations of 18 MLLMs, additional controlled diagnostic experiments, annotation audits and downstream VLA correlation analyses.

M1.justification: The core DAG-based world simulator remains. Its supplied scoring prompt changes from flexible standard-mode matching to explicit greedy, same-referent and per-arm matching, adds empty-goal completion handling, and removes diagnostic output fields (v1 Figure 26; v2 Figure 29). These refine the existing evaluator.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained RoboBench coverage, v2 evaluates downstream robotic control on CALVIN and LIBERO-10. This adds sequential manipulation and unseen-scene generalization to the earlier offline cognitive evaluations (Section 5.3 and Appendix D.5).

E2.justification: Tables 3–6 change from 14 to 18 evaluated models, adding twelve and removing eight. Additions include GPT-5.4, Claude-Opus-4.7, Gemini-3.1-Pro and MiMo-Embodied-7B; removals include GPT-4o-Mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet and Qwen2.5-VL-72B. The text-only reference changes from GPT-4o to GPT-5.4.

E3.justification: Affordance evaluation changes from point/trajectory prediction scored using distance and RMSE to multiple-choice accuracy. Reported sample counts also change. New downstream protocols specify CALVIN ABC-D and LIBERO-10 training/evaluation settings. Q1 aggregation is inconsistently described in v2: Section 4 specifies a composite, whereas Appendix D.2 says main results report node scores.

E4.justification: v2 adds evaluator robustness across four judges and three prompts on 200 items, a paired 100-episode intent-scaffolding ablation, annotation-noise tests on 30 items, a 50-item instruction audit, and downstream correlation analyses. The earlier human-alignment study and qualitative cases are retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Beyond the retained human-alignment Pearson correlations, v2 introduces ICC(2,k) and Cronbach's alpha for evaluator agreement, correlation p-values in Table 12, and mean-plus/minus reporting for the instruction audit. These substantially expand statistical reporting without establishing repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 3–6 extensively revise scores and rankings; for example, GPT-4o's Table 4 planning average changes from 37.74 to 73.46. These are not established same-setting gains given the protocol revisions. Tables 8–12 add robustness, ablation and downstream findings; human-alignment correlations remain 0.83 versus 0.73.

T1.justification: The DAG formalization and central planning equations remain. v2 Figure 29 extends the completion-score definition with an explicit empty-critical-state case returning 10, which v1's ratio formula does not specify. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v1 principally claims comprehensive cognitive assessment and improved planning evaluation. v2 additionally claims that RoboBench abilities predict downstream VLA performance and guide backbone selection, making practical predictive validity a contribution in the introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations linking CALVIN performance to perception and LIBERO performance to affordances, while acknowledging the latter correlation is not conventionally significant. It also interprets the CoT ablation as an intent-grounding limitation, discusses output-format sensitivity, and limits that conclusion to the tested frontier models.

D1.justification: v2 adds substantial downstream implementation information, including ActionQuery/MLP adaptation, inputs, training budgets, learning rates, batch sizes and action chunks. It expands scoring and annotation-validation details and updates model identifiers. However, v1's 20-annotator count and 438-item human-alignment sample size are no longer stated.

R1.justification: Section 2, Table 1 and Appendix B add substantive comparisons with BEAR and ECBench. References also add VLM4VLA, CALVIN and newer model reports. These extend the existing embodied-benchmark positioning rather than replace it.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution statements, performance discussion and Q1 scoring prompt are substantially rewritten. Separate error-analysis and human-alignment subsections become an integrated In-Depth Analysis section; the appendix hierarchy is reorganized and references move behind the supplementary material.

P2.justification: The publication template, typography, table placement and highlighting change throughout. Figure 1 gains a downstream panel; the former Figure 6 is split and recombined with existing error cases. New correlation plots, robustness tables and annotation-quality tables substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable evaluator controls, annotation audits and downstream validation absent from v1. However, its conflicting descriptions of Q1 aggregation leave the revised leaderboard's meaning unresolved, and the affordance metric change is not reconciled with unchanged human scores. These uncertainties concern the benchmark's central measurements, preventing a reliable net quality judgment despite the added evidence.
